description: A PostHog project and its main settings. Deleting the resource deletes the PostHog project and all of its data (events, persons, recordings, insights, flags and so on); it cannot be undone.

ApiKey.description: PostHog personal API key (phx_...) with the scopes this resource type needs. Pass it with a dynamic reference such as {{resolve:ssm-secure:/posthog/api-key}} when calling SetTypeConfiguration; never put it in plain text.

BaseUrl.description: PostHog API host. Leave unset for PostHog Cloud US (https://us.posthog.com); use https://eu.posthog.com for PostHog Cloud EU, or your instance URL when self-hosting.

OrganizationId.description: ID (UUID) of the PostHog organization the project belongs to.

Id.description: The PostHog project ID. Use it as ProjectId for project-scoped PostHog resources.

Name.description: Project name. Must be unique within the organization (case-insensitive).

ProductDescription.description: Short description of what the project is about, used as context by PostHog AI features.

Tags.description: Labels applied to the project. PostHog trims and lowercases them.

AppUrls.description: URLs of the sites and apps that send data to this project (used by the toolbar and heatmaps).

AnonymizeIps.description: When true, PostHog drops the IP address from every ingested event.

Timezone.description: IANA timezone used for date-based filters and reporting, e.g. America/Los_Angeles. PostHog defaults to UTC.

WeekStartDay.description: First day of the week for date range filters: 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

BaseCurrency.description: ISO 4217 currency code used for revenue analytics, e.g. EUR. PostHog defaults to USD.

BusinessModel.description: Whether the project serves B2B or B2C customers (b2b, b2c or other). Used to optimize default UI layouts.

AutocaptureOptOut.description: Disables posthog-js autocapture (clicks, page views) when true.

AutocaptureExceptionsOptIn.description: Enables automatic capture of JavaScript exceptions via the SDK.

AutocaptureWebVitalsOptIn.description: Enables automatic capture of Core Web Vitals performance metrics.

CaptureConsoleLogOptIn.description: Enables capturing browser console logs alongside session replays.

CapturePerformanceOptIn.description: Enables capturing performance timing and network requests.

CaptureDeadClicks.description: Enables capturing clicks that had no effect.

HeatmapsOptIn.description: Enables heatmap recording on pages that use posthog-js.

SurveysOptIn.description: Enables displaying surveys via posthog-js on allowed origins.

SessionRecordingOptIn.description: Enables session replay recording for this project.

SessionRecordingSampleRate.description: Fraction of sessions to record, as a decimal string between 0.00 and 1.00 (e.g. 0.1 = 10%).

SessionRecordingMinimumDurationMilliseco.description: Skip saving sessions shorter than this many milliseconds.

SessionRecordingRetentionPeriod.description: How long to retain new session recordings: 30d, 90d, 1y or 5y (availability depends on plan).

RecordingDomains.description: Origins permitted to record session replays and heatmaps. Empty allows all origins.

DataAttributes.description: Element attributes that posthog-js captures as action identifiers, e.g. data-attr.

PersonDisplayNameProperties.description: Ordered list of person properties used to render a person's display name in the UI.

TestAccountFilters.description: JSON array of property filters that identify internal/test traffic to exclude from insights (use Fn::ToJsonString), e.g. [{"key": "email", "value": "@example.com", "operator": "not_icontains", "type": "person"}].

TestAccountFiltersDefaultChecked.description: When true, new insights exclude internal/test users by default.

PathCleaningFilters.description: JSON array of regex rewrite rules that collapse dynamic path segments before URLs are shown in paths (use Fn::ToJsonString), e.g. [{"regex": "/user/\\d+", "alias": "/user/<id>"}].

ApiToken.description: The project API key (public token, phc_...) that PostHog SDKs use to send events.

ApiHost.description: Host the PostHog SDKs send events to (their api_host option).
